chunks: I said to him: 'What is the meaning of the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): "The lowest of them acts by their covenant of protection"?' He said: 'If an army of Muslims besieges a people of the polytheists, and a man approaches and says: "Give me security until I meet your companion and debate him," and the lowest of them grants him the security, then it becomes obligatory upon the most superior of them to honor it.'

key_terms.الأمان: aman — safe-conduct, security guarantee granted to a non-Muslim to enter Muslim territory or engage in negotiations
key_terms.الذمة: dhimma — covenant of protection; the obligation incumbent on Muslims to protect those under their guarantee
key_terms.الوفاء: wafa' — loyalty, fulfillment of a pledge or covenant; a cardinal virtue in Islamic ethics

ai.seo_question: What does the Islamic ruling say about a low-ranking soldier granting security (aman) to the enemy?
ai.summary: This hadith records a question posed to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) by al-Sakuni about the meaning of a Prophetic saying regarding military safe-conduct (aman). The Imam explains that if even the lowest-ranking soldier in a Muslim army grants security to an enemy combatant seeking dialogue, all higher-ranking officers — including the commander — are legally bound to uphold that pledge. This ruling reflects the Islamic principle that a covenant of protection, once given in good faith by any Muslim, is binding on the entire community, ensuring the integrity of Islamic military ethics and the sanctity of pledged word.
